payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a release cut's tag is not pushed, every install pin on main names a tag that exists on origin.
When a release tag is pushed, the install pins on main name that tag.
payload.description:
## Context
When a release is cut but its tag is not pushed, I want the install pins on main to keep naming a published tag, so nobody who installs from the README or the site gets a missing tag.

## Finding
2026-11-17: basicly release 0.46.2 made version commit 8a0bc4a8, which rewrote the install pins (README.md, site/index.html, .scripts/bootstrap.sh, .scripts/bootstrap.ps1, docs) from v0.46.1 to v0.46.2. The release-process rule pushes main first and the tag only after green CI on the version commit. Quality-gates 43965947002 on 8a0bc4a8 failed, so v0.46.2 was never pushed and was deleted locally. Main and the Pages site (deployed 2026-11-16 22:01 UTC) therefore named a tag that does not exist, and an install from them fails until a later release publishes.

## Fix
Options: push the version commit and tag together only after CI on a candidate; or keep pins on the published tag until the tag push succeeds. Not claimed.
payload.title: Keep install pins on main pointing at a published tag when a release cut stops before the tag push

payload.text: [2026-11-17, Orchestrator] Required check: the release gate refuses a commit that moves install pins to a version whose tag does not exist on the remote. Decision: no separate pin revert now; 0.46.3 rewrites the pins. If 0.46.3 is not published by 23:30 UTC on 2026-11-17, the Orchestrator puts a pin revert to v0.46.1 before the owner as a deploy.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
docs/design holds the session-state design and names herdr's licence and the version measured.
Every herdr or vendor fact in it names its source or the probe that establishes it.
It contains no machine path, user name, host name, pane id or private session name.
payload.description:
## Context
A person who runs Claude Code, Codex and Copilot sessions in herdr tabs cannot tell which session works, waits for an answer or has finished. herdr already classifies every agent pane from the screen; a reporter adds a short state label from each vendor's hooks. The design is reviewed privately; this task writes its public form in docs/design beside the orchestrator kit draft, and records herdr's licence, shipped mechanism and independent evidence as the External Review rule requires.

payload.title: Session state: public design document

payload.acceptance_criteria:
S2: on scratch panes in the states working, idle and done, a state label report leaves agent_status unchanged and a clear removes the label.
S4: a scratch Claude Code session records whether a background shell and a monitor appear in Stop background_tasks and whether their completion fires a hook.
S5: the reporter's hook run for each event stays under 50 ms on the measuring machine, with the median and maximum recorded.
payload.description:
## Context
The reporter relies on three facts that need no person to observe: a state label leaves herdr's agent_status unchanged (S2), Claude Code's Stop hook lists background work and a background completion fires a hook (S4), and a hook run stays under 50 ms (S5). They run on scratch panes and a scratch project; S5 and part of S2 were measured on 2026-11-17 with herdr 0.9.5.
payload.requirements: No vendor credential is collected, stored or brokered (requirement R0 of basicly-qpr2xmr).
payload.title: Session state: probes S2, S4 and S5 without the owner

S3: for a Claude permission prompt, a question, a sandbox network prompt, an automatic-mode ask, a Codex approval and a Copilot approval, herdr's state is recorded.
S6: whether herdr gives a sound, an OS notice or a tab highlight when a pane turns blocked is recorded.
payload.description:
## Context
Three facts need a person and a second pane: where state labels show in herdr's tab list and pane frame (S1), whether herdr shows blocked for each kind of prompt of each vendor (S3), and whether herdr itself alerts on blocked (S6). They run in one booked session with the owner, together with the orchestrator kit's P6.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
The herdr adapter builds the argument list pane id first, with --source, a --seq from time_ns and each label as one argument.
When herdr is missing, hangs, or the input or pane id is invalid, the reporter exits 0 within its 1-second timeout.
The reporter writes nothing to standard output, so it never emits a permission decision.
A label holds the tool name and the first word of the command, at most 80 characters, with control characters removed.
Without HERDR_ENV, the reporter runs no process and exits 0.
A hook run of the installed reporter stays under 50 ms on the measuring machine.
payload.description:
## Context
From Claude Code hooks, the reporter sets or clears a herdr state label on its own pane: cleared at SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, a needs-you label at PermissionRequest cleared at PostToolUse, and a paused label at Stop when background work is listed. It lives in packages/basicly-orch (orch_state/reporter.py and orch_state/herdr.py), not in a kit, because it runs a process. Without herdr it does nothing. The label names the tool and the first word of its command only, since the tab list is visible to anyone at the screen.
payload.requirements: No vendor credential is collected, stored or brokered (requirement R0 of basicly-qpr2xmr).
payload.title: Session state: reporter and herdr adapter in basicly-orch

payload.acceptance_criteria:
The owner approved the exact settings diff before it was written, and the approval is recorded on this task.
After installation, the five Claude hook entries call the installed reporter and herdr's own entry is unchanged.
Removing exactly those entries and uninstalling the uv tool returns the settings to their earlier bytes.
payload.description:
## Context
The reporter runs from separate hook entries beside herdr's own hook file, never inside it, because herdr rewrites its file on update. Before a basicly release carries the package, it is installed as a uv tool and its Claude hook entries go into the user settings, which every session loads, so the owner sees the exact diff and approves it first. Codex and Copilot follow after probe S3, each with its own diff.
